 Microsoft doesn't believe they are 'dealing with a cyber attack' LIVE Updated 12 mins ago Microsoft outage live: Claude AI goes down for thousands as Outlook and Teams issues continue
 Thousands of people across the UK have woken up to problems accessing Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot amid a global outage affecting millions of users
 Add to preferred sources Comments News Sophie Huskisson Political Correspondent , Eliana Nunes News Reporter , Tannur Anders UK & World News Reporter and Helena Vesty UK & World News Reporter Updated 15:15, 13 Nov 2026 NHS GP practices, pharmacies, police forces and schools have been hit by a major Microsoft outage that has disrupted services for millions of people around the world.
 The tech giant has been battling widespread disruption to Outlook, Teams, its AI assistant Copilot and its cloud-based subscription service Microsoft 365 , among other services, since yesterday evening. Thousands of UK users reported being unable to access their emails and carry out their work and daily tasks this morning. GMB Union has claimed the Microsoft outage is preventing 111 and 999 services from referring patient details as they normally would, creating a "massive backlog".
 In the UK , Downdetector had recorded nearly 8,000 reports of problems with Outlook, around 3,800 with Microsoft 365 and 1,300 with Teams at around 9am today. Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT were also affected by the Microsoft outage, with more than 3,770 UK reports of problems with Claude having been logged on Downdetector at 10.15am.
 Microsoft said the fault stems from infrastructure issues within Exchange Online and is not the result of a cyber attack.
 ‌ 
 New Updates Key Events
 Microsoft: 'We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress in Europe' View Post OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude affected by Microsoft outage View Post GMB Union: Microsoft outage stopping 111 and 999 from referring patient det… View Post Millions of people across 74 countries affected by Microsoft outage View Post Microsoft reports 'early stabilization' as 'recovery actions continue' View Post Schools and universities report that their email services are down View Post Some airlines experiencing communication disruptions View Post Cause of outage is 'elevated load' View Post Servers operating overnight but crashed again View Post Outage not caused by cyber-security incident View Post Attempts to address outage 'not taking as expected' View Post Today 15:13 GMT Users complain they can't receive emails more than 20 hours into outage
 Some users have complained they are still unable to receive emails as the outage passes the 20-hour mark.
 It comes after Microsoft said in its latest update that some people "may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery" as they continue fixing the problem.
 Content cannot be displayed without consent Comments Zahra Khaliq Today 14:32 GMT Microsoft says its email services are 'approaching normal levels'
 Microsoft has said its email services are "approaching normal levels" more than 20 hours after the outage began.
 It said: "We’re continuing to see improvements in service availability, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.
 "Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery continues."
 The outage began on Thursday evening (Image: Yui Mok/Press Association) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 14:13 GMT Computer science professor explains what went wrong
 James Ferryman, professor of computer science at the University of Reading, said the fault stems from a system called Exchange Online, which handles the emails and calendars behind Outlook and is also relied upon by Teams and Copilot.
 Prof Ferryman told the Mirror: "Think back to September, when a fault in the UK’s air traffic control computers led to more than a thousand flights being cancelled. One system that every airport depends on went wrong, and the effects spread across the country. Even once it was fixed, planes couldn’t all take off at once. The backlog had to be cleared carefully.
 "This is similar. Microsoft says the part of its computers that sets up a secure connection with your device got swamped. As some machines dropped out, the rest took the strain, while millions of phones and laptops kept trying to reconnect. So it has to be brought back a bit at a time."
 Professor James Ferryman (Image: University of Reading) 
 He added: "We still don’t know what set it off. Microsoft says there is no sign of a cyber attack. The fall-out is clear. Schools and councils have asked people to phone instead. Some NHS staff have been locked out of email. For businesses, the lost time could cost tens of millions of pounds in the UK alone.
 "The lesson is how much of daily life now runs through a few big computer systems. Every workplace needs a plan B."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 14:01 GMT Are flights affected by the Microsoft outage?
 While a broad range of services in the UK and around the world have been disrupted by the Microsoft outage, the aviation sector appears to have been largely unaffected.
 Aviation outlets are reporting that airlines in India have faced disruption.
 Low-cost carrier SpiceJet was forced to cancel around 22 flights today, according to Simple Flying, which cited data from FlightAware.
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 13:46 GMT Is Amazon affected by the Microsoft outage? 
 Amazon does not appear to have been affected by the Microsoft outage. Yesterday, Amazon Web Services (AWS) confirmed it was "operating normally", saying reports of an outage affecting its platforms were "inaccurate".
 Content cannot be displayed without consent 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 13:35 GMT Microsoft outage has been taking place for 20 hours
 An outage has been affecting Microsoft for more than 20 hours.
 However, Microsoft has just published an update, reporting "sustained improvements across much of Europe".
 It said: "We’re seeing continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.
 "Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as mitigation continues across remaining affected infrastructure.
 "Our focus remains on stabilizing recovered infrastructure, completing mitigation in remaining impacted areas, and reducing delayed email queues and backlogs while we validate service consistency across connection methods."
 Microsoft is facing an outage affecting more than 70 countries (Image: ANP/Shutterstock) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 12:55 GMT Microsoft: 'We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress in Europe'
 Microsoft has said it is seeing "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" as some users in the UK and elsewhere around the world begin to regain access to their Outlook emails and other Microsoft services.
 In its latest status update, the tech giant said: "We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress in Europe, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure.
 "Japan remains comparatively more stable, while North America is also improving; however, some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 12:52 GMT Latest from Government on Microsoft outage
 Contingency plans are in place for disrupted Microsoft services as the Government works to establish the "full picture" of the impact, Downing Street has said.
 The Prime Minister’s deputy spokeswoman said: "We’re working with departments and with Microsoft to establish the full picture, and where services are disrupted, departments have contingency arrangements in place.
 "You’ll obviously appreciate this is an ongoing situation, but in the meantime, people are encouraged to follow advice on the services they require for alternative ways to get in touch."
 The spokeswoman said ministers are being kept regularly updated and that a "range of services" are experiencing disruption as parts of the Government use Microsoft.
 She added: "Frontline services have their own contingency arrangements, and departments are working to make sure essential services keep running."
 (Image: ANP/Shutterstock) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 12:46 GMT Microsoft outage fuels Friday the 13th jokes on social media
 It has not been lost on social media users that the Microsoft outage affecting millions of people across 74 countries is taking place on Friday the 13th - widely regarded as an unlucky day.
 The outage, which has disrupted key Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot, technically began at around 6pm GMT on Thursday.
 One X user joked: "It’s Friday 13th & Microsoft suffer a huge outage surely that’s all the explanation anyone needs?"
 "Friday the 13th strikes again!" another chimed in.
 Analysis published by Rightmove suggests that people tend to avoid moving house on Friday the 13th.
 The property website analysed Land Registry data dating back to 1995 and found that Friday the 13th is typically the quietest Friday for home moves, despite Fridays generally being popular for moves as people look to settle in over the weekend.
 The analysis also found that the 13th is, on average, the quietest day of the month for property completions.
 A Rightmove spokesperson said its website is working as usual, adding: "We’re hearing that agents are working hard over the phone to help those home movers who are completing today."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 12:24 GMT NHS urges patients to attend appointments unless told otherwise
 The NHS has urged patients to attend appointments unless told otherwise, and to use 999 in an emergency and otherwise contact 111, use NHS 111 online or visit their local pharmacy.
 A spokesperson said: "With the global Microsoft issue inevitably having a disruptive impact for staff, local NHS services are enacting long-standing measures to manage IT outages and ensure critical services and appointments can continue for patients today - including using other IT systems or paper records where possible.
 "Patients should continue to use 999 in an emergency, and otherwise use 111, 111 online, or their local pharmacy, and come forward for appointments unless told otherwise."
 As we reported earlier, GMB Union claimed the Microsoft outage is preventing 111 and 999 services from referring patient details as they normally would, creating a "massive backlog".
 Rachel Harrison, GMB national secretary, said: "The Microsoft data outage is having a serious impact across ambulance and NHS trusts.
 "Those who work in 111 and 999 services are unable to refer patient details in the normal way which is creating a massive backlog and has the potential for chaos. Luckily emergency and life-threatening callouts appear to be unaffected."
 (Image: WalesOnline/ Rob Browne) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 12:17 GMT More than 3,770 reports of Claude issues logged as Microsoft outage continues
 More than 3,770 UK reports of problems with Anthropic's Claude had been logged on outage-tracking website Downdetector at around 10.15am. Reports have steadily declined since, but Claude services remain affected.
 Claude reported issues with its Microsoft 365 connector yesterday evening, with the latest update on its status page published at around 10.30pm.
 It said: "This issue is caused by a Microsoft 365 service incident, and mail, calendar and search tools in the Microsoft 365 connector are still failing for most requests. Claude for Outlook remains affected."
 UK reports of problems with AI chatbot Claude (Image: Downdetector) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 12:04 GMT Rail passengers may be unable to access tickets by email
 National Rail has said the Microsoft outage may be affecting customers' ability to access their train tickets via email. Those affected bought e-tickets after the outage began.
 Customers affected may still be able to access their tickets on the website or app where they bought their tickets and by logging into their accounts, National Rail said.
 Customers who checked out as a guest rather than logging into an account are advised to contact their ticket retailer directly if they are unable to access tickets. Those still unable to access tickets are advised to speak to onboard or station staff.
 Rail passengers may be experiencing difficulties accessing their train tickets by email (file image) (Image: Getty Images) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 11:48 GMT Microsoft says it's making 'progress' with service recovery - starting with Asia Pacific
 Microsoft said it has made "additional progress toward service recovery", starting with the Asia Pacific region and gradually working across other regions worldwide to resolve its widespread outage.
 In its latest Microsoft 365 status update, it said: "We’ve made additional progress toward service recovery, with recovery actions completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region.
 "Traffic is being gradually restored, and we’re seeing improvements in key customer scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing. However, some users may continue to experience intermittent issues."
 Microsoft added: "Our focus is now on extending these recovery actions across affected infrastructure in other regions, while continuing stabilisation efforts and adding supporting capacity to improve service consistency."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 11:44 GMT Microsoft outage affects Asda services
 Asda has said on its website: "Due to an ongoing Global Microsoft Service Disruption, new customers are unable to complete the registration process.
 "Customers are also unable to perform password reset or email change operations."
 We are looking into whether other major supermarkets have been affected.
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 11:34 GMT OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude affected by Microsoft outage
 Artificial intelligence (AI) software services have also been impacted by the Microsoft outage, with OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude experiencing problems.
 OpenAI said in its latest update: "We’re investigating an issue with Microsoft connectors where new connections may be broken and tools are not working as expected. We’ll share an update when we know more."
 Anthropic said in its latest update that Claude was experiencing problems with its Microsoft 365 connector, adding that its mail, calendar and search tools were still failing for most requests. It said Claude for Outlook was also affected.
 AI services have also been affected by the Microsoft outage (Image: Getty Images) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 11:18 GMT Microsoft outage affects Great Western Railway ticket emails
 Great Western Railway has warned travellers that the Microsoft outage is affecting its ability to automatically email ticket confirmations this morning.
 Content cannot be displayed without consent Comments Eliana Nunes Today 11:12 GMT GMB Union: Microsoft outage stopping 111 and 999 from referring patient details, creating 'massive backlog'
 The Microsoft outage is preventing 111 and 999 services from referring patient details as they normally would, according to the GMB union.
 The disruption is creating a "massive backlog", although emergency callouts "appear to be unaffected".
 GMB National Secretary Rachel Harrison said: "The Microsoft data outage is having a serious impact across ambulance and NHS trusts.
 "Those who work in 111 and 999 services are unable to refer patient details in the normal way which is creating a massive backlog and has the potential for chaos.
 "Luckily emergency and life-threatening call-outs appear to be unaffected."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 11:09 GMT Microsoft outage is affecting some NHS services, particularly access to email
 NHS leaders are "working hard to minimise disruption" amid the Microsoft outage.
 Sir Ciarán Devane, chief executive of the NHS Alliance, said: "The Microsoft outage is affecting some NHS services, notably access to email, but it appears that all clinical and operational systems are working effectively.
 "NHS leaders and their teams are working hard to minimise disruption, maintain essential services and support staff and patients who may be affected.
 "Their priority is, as always, to ensure patient safety and continuity of care. NHS organisations have workarounds in place when email is unavailable, so contingencies are in place to manage situations like this."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 11:00 GMT Reports of Outlook outage spike as Brits start work
 Almost 8,000 UK reports of Outlook problems had been recorded on outage-tracking website Downdetector at around 9am - shortly after many people started their working day.
 (Image: Downdetector) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 10:48 GMT Millions of people across 74 countries affected by Microsoft outage
 Users from 74 countries reported issues with Microsoft services in the space of an hour yesterday, according to outage-tracking website Downdetector.
 More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, according to the tech giant's website.
 Problems with Microsoft were reported from countries including the US, India and New Zealand (Image: Daniel Dayment/SWNS) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 10:39 GMT Schools tell parents not to email to report absence
 Ballifield Primary School in Sheffield said in a post on X that it has no access to its emails due to the Microsoft Outlook outage.
 Like other schools affected by the disruption, it advised parents and carers to phone the school if they need to report an absence or get in touch for any other reason.
 With many UK organisations - such as councils - heavily reliant on emails, self-service portals and cloud-based platforms, today's outage is likely to cause significant disruption for both staff and the public.
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 10:27 GMT Councils unable to access their emails
 Social media platform X is flooded with posts from schools, universities and councils reporting that their Outlook email services are unavailable or experiencing disruption.
 South Tyneside Council has said it is currently unable to access its emails. Durham County Council, Birmingham City Council, Barnet Council, Fife Council and Cork County Council have also reported difficulties.
 Content cannot be displayed without consent Comments Eliana Nunes Today 10:11 GMT 'SEN school where I work is in carnage'
 We're now hearing from some of you who have been affected by the Microsoft outage.
 Laurie said the SEN (Special Educational Needs) school where she works "is in carnage", adding that systems including CPOMS, child-in-need backup records and first aid registers are all down. "You name it it's gone," she said.
 Outlook user Julie said she had not received "any emails today" - "not even junk mail" - adding that the service was "very hit and miss" yesterday too. Claire said her children's school emails are not working.
 You can share your experience by leaving a comment on this post on our Facebook page or this post on our X account .
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 10:03 GMT Microsoft reports 'early stabilization' as 'recovery actions continue'
 Microsoft has said in an update: "We’re seeing early stabilization and capacity improvements as recovery actions continue. To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 09:49 GMT Microsoft outage: How has it affected your day?
 Have you been affected by the ongoing Microsoft outage? If so, we want to hear how it has disrupted your day and work.
 You can share your experience by leaving a comment under this post on our Facebook page or this post on our X account .
 If you have access to a non-Microsoft email account, you can also get in touch at webnews@mirror.co.uk .
 More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps (Image: David Talukdar/Shutterstock) 
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 09:31 GMT Schools and universities report that their email services are down
 UK schools and universities, many of which rely on Microsoft Outlook for their email services, have also been affected by the ongoing outage.
 Bishop Fox's Community School in Taunton, Somerset, and City St George's, University of London, are among the institutions to have reported on X that their email services are currently down.
 Content cannot be displayed without consent Comments Eliana Nunes Today 09:11 GMT NHS GP practices and pharmacies hit by global Microsoft outage
 We're now hearing about the impact of the ongoing Microsoft outage on health services across the UK this morning.
 NHS North East and North Cumbria has reported that GP surgeries and some hospitals in the region have been affected.
 But the NHS board added that "there is currently no known imapct on 999 or other emergency services".
 A spokesperson for the UK National Pharmacy Association told the Mirror that the outage is disrupting access to the NHS email system.
 "This affects pharmacy’s ability to communicate with GP practices and some patients," the spokesperson said. "Please bear with your pharmacy teams today, where waits may be longer than normal and there may be delays to some prescriptions."
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 09:05 GMT NHS doctor says Microsoft outage will be 'very disruptive today'
 Dr Tim Frank, an NHS GP in Penzance, Cornwall, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he has been unable to receive emails overnight and this morning.
 He said the disruption is particularly concerning because Microsoft services are "central" to primary care and community operations in the area.
 "This is going to be very disruptive today and Fridays are always a heavily laden day due to the upcoming weekend," he said.
 Comments Eliana Nunes Today 08:53 GMT Microsoft outage leaves millions unable to access emails or Teams
 A major Microsoft outage has caused widespread disruption across the world, with millions of people unable to access their emails on Outlook and Teams.
 Microsoft 365 services have been impacted by "connectivity problems". These include the messaging service Teams, Outlook emails, some aspects of its Cloud services and the AI software Copilot.
 Users have reported varying levels of access, with some unable to send emails or others not able to send messages via Teams.
 The tech giant has provided updates on official Microsoft 365 accounts but earlier Microsoft directed people to a page on its website for updates. However, users complained the page did not load.
 Multiple governments around the world have reported Microsoft outages, including in India, Japan and Australia - where the country's spy and federal police agencies said they have been left unable to send emails.
 Read more on everything we know about the outage here .
 Comments Elizabeta Ranxburgaj Today 08:44 GMT 'I want to see this fixed. It’s on Microsoft to do so,' says Government minister
 Defence Minister Luke Pollard has told Times Radio this morning: "Government engineers and the systems are working with Microsoft at the moment. I would expect that to be able to be detailed throughout the day.
 "But as more people come online with their working days shortly, I think there’ll be sadly more people frustrated with the system. But I hope Microsoft can sort it out."
 He continued: "So we’re looking across Government. Forgive me, this is not a portfolio that I am responsible for, but the understanding that I have from Downing Street on this is that Government systems are being looked at in relation to Microsoft, in making sure that we have the resilience that we need for the Government.
 "But there’ll be lots of people who are trying to access their work systems and their systems every day who will be deeply frustrated by this. I get that frustration.
 "That’s why we’ve already been in touch with Microsoft. The dialogue between our cyber resilience teams across Government and Microsoft continues. I want to see this fixed. It’s on Microsoft to do so. I hope they can get there very soon."
 Defence Minister Luke Pollard (Image: Toby Shepheard/AFP via Getty Images)
